## Overview

The `WOA` provides typed, robust Python clients for Zoho enterprise services,
built-in OAuth2 token caching, Catalyst token switching, rate-limiting handlers,
and security sanitizers.

## Quick Start

### Connecting to Zoho Books
```python
from zoho import ZohoBooksAPI, ZohoOAuth2Manager

oauth = ZohoOAuth2Manager(
    client_id='your_client_id',
    client_secret='your_client_secret',
    refresh_token='your_refresh_token',
    domain='in'
)

books = ZohoBooksAPI(
    access_token=oauth.get_access_token(),
    organization_id='123456789',
    domain='in',
    token_refresh_callback=oauth.get_access_token
)

# Auto-paginated bill iterator
for bill in books.bills.list_iter(resource_key='bills'):
    print(bill['bill_number'], bill['total'])
```

### Connecting to Zoho Inventory
```python
from zoho import ZohoInventoryAPI

inventory = ZohoInventoryAPI(
    access_token='your_access_token',
    organization_id='123456789',
    domain='in'
)

for item in inventory.items.list_iter(resource_key='items'):
    print(item['name'], item.get('actual_available_stock'))
```

### Public API Exports

All primary client classes and exceptions can be imported directly from the top-level package:
```python
from zoho import (
    ZohoBooksAPI, ZohoBooksError,
    ZohoInventoryAPI, ZohoInventoryError,
    ZohoAnalyticsAPI, ZohoAnalyticsError,
    ZohoERPAPI, ZohoERPError,
    ZohoCreatorAPI, ZohoCreatorError,
    ZohoMailAPI, ZohoMailError,
    ZohoWorkdriveAPI,
    ZohoSheetAPI,
    ZohoCliqAPI,
    ZohoOAuth2Manager, CatalystAuth, HttpTokenProvider,
    ZohoError, ZohoAuthError,
    sanitize_filename, resolve_output_path,
)
```
